request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (5,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `PAY_0`: repayment status in September 2005, the latest month (-1 paid in full, 1 to 9 months of payment delay; -2 and 0 are not in the data dictionary, commonly read as no consumption and revolving credit used).
  Share of importance 36.3% (95% band 24.1% to 52.1%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.35; 1: +0.4; >= 2: +2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +2.36, 95% band [+2.12, +2.73]).
- `LIMIT_BAL`: amount of the given credit in NT dollars, individual and family (supplementary) credit.
  Share of importance 23.2% (95% band 13.5% to 24.9%); rank 2 to 3 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 89999: +0.4; >= 90000: -0.28 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -1.13, 95% band [-1.27, -0.44]).
- `PAY_AMT1`: amount paid in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 13.5% (95% band 7.0% to 19.6%); rank 2 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 2612: +0.1; >= 2613: -0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.69, 95% band [-0.92, -0.22]).
- `BILL_AMT1`: amount of the bill statement in September 2005, the latest month, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 4.1% (95% band 0.0% to 5.9%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.21, 95% band [-0.14, +0.31]).
- `AGE`: age in years.
  Share of importance 2.6% (95% band 0.0% to 6.1%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.15, 95% band [-0.11, +0.47]).
- `PAY_AMT3`: amount paid in July 2005, two months before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 2.0% (95% band 0.0% to 3.9%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.07, 95% band [-0.16, +0.12]).
- `BILL_AMT2`: amount of the bill statement in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.0% to 5.3%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.10, 95% band [-0.19, +0.39]).
- `PAY_AMT2`: amount paid in August 2005, the month before, in NT dollars.
  Share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.0% to 7.1%); rank 4 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.03, 95% band [-0.42, +0.09]).
- `EDUCATION`: education (1 graduate school, 2 university, 3 high school, 4 others; 0, 5 and 6 are not in the data dictionary).
  Share of importance 0.2% (95% band 0.0% to 2.4%); rank 5 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.01, 95% band [-0.09, +0.09]).

Interactions: the model has 22 pairs. The larger ones:
- `PAY_0 & BILL_AMT1`: share of importance 2.2% (95% band 0.0% to 4.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +1.79 (95% band +1.09 to +2.64) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +2.42 (95% band +2.00 to +2.81) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.10 (95% band -0.24 to +0.38) when `PAY_0` = -2, +0.73 (95% band -0.06 to +1.58) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & AGE`: share of importance 1.9% (95% band 0.0% to 2.7%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -0.87 (95% band -1.25 to -0.40) when `AGE` = 23, -1.25 (95% band -1.36 to -0.45) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.37 (95% band -0.03 to +0.62) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.01 (95% band -0.26 to +0.37) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_0 & LIMIT_BAL`: share of importance 1.7% (95% band 1.2% to 5.1%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.29 (95% band +2.01 to +2.89) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +2.45 (95% band +1.66 to +2.86) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.16 (95% band -1.29 to -0.41) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.99 (95% band -1.56 to -0.28) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_AMT1 & BILL_AMT2`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 1.9%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.77 (95% band -1.05 to -0.18) when `BILL_AMT2` = 0, -0.87 (95% band -1.02 to -0.23) when `BILL_AMT2` = 196,000.
  Effect of `BILL_AMT2` from 0 to 196,000: +0.26 (95% band -0.24 to +0.47) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +0.16 (95% band -0.36 to +0.39) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
- `BILL_AMT1 & AGE`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 2.5%).
  Effect of `BILL_AMT1` from 0 to 201,000: +0.27 (95% band -0.16 to +0.47) when `AGE` = 23, +0.13 (95% band -0.41 to +0.28) when `AGE` = 53.
  Effect of `AGE` from 23 to 53: +0.20 (95% band -0.07 to +0.44) when `BILL_AMT1` = 0, +0.06 (95% band -0.69 to +0.39) when `BILL_AMT1` = 201,000.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT2`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.0% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.44 (95% band +2.11 to +2.84) when `PAY_AMT2` = 0, +2.14 (95% band +1.73 to +2.74) when `PAY_AMT2` = 17,900.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT2` from 0 to 17,900: -0.01 (95% band -0.44 to +0.11) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.31 (95% band -0.93 to +0.14) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `PAY_0 & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 1.2% (95% band 0.6% to 4.0%).
  Effect of `PAY_0` from -2 to 2: +2.19 (95% band +1.81 to +2.61) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, +2.46 (95% band +2.15 to +3.00) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.75 (95% band -1.02 to -0.30) when `PAY_0` = -2, -0.48 (95% band -0.85 to +0.02) when `PAY_0` = 2.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT1`: share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.0% to 2.4%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.16 (95% band -1.32 to -0.33) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -1.17 (95% band -1.30 to -0.45) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.70 (95% band -0.97 to -0.23) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, -0.71 (95% band -1.02 to -0.22) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `LIMIT_BAL & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.0% to 3.3%).
  Effect of `LIMIT_BAL` from 20,000 to 430,000: -1.09 (95% band -1.23 to -0.37) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, -1.16 (95% band -1.41 to -0.44) when `PAY_AMT3` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 18,100: +0.10 (95% band -0.11 to +0.35) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 20,000, +0.03 (95% band -0.37 to +0.07) when `LIMIT_BAL` = 430,000.
- `PAY_AMT1 & PAY_AMT3`: share of importance 0.5% (95% band 0.0% to 1.7%).
  Effect of `PAY_AMT1` from 0 to 17,000: -0.61 (95% band -0.92 to -0.21) when `PAY_AMT3` = 0, -0.83 (95% band -1.17 to -0.22) when `PAY_AMT3` = 18,100.
  Effect of `PAY_AMT3` from 0 to 18,100: +0.19 (95% band -0.17 to +0.36) when `PAY_AMT1` = 0, -0.03 (95% band -0.49 to +0.14) when `PAY_AMT1` = 17,000.
- 12 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 2.8%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mainly by repayment status in the latest month, September 2005, which accounts for about 36% of its importance, with a plausible range of roughly 24% to 52%."},{"id":2,"text":"Applicants who were already behind on payments (a delay of 2 months or more) carry a much higher predicted risk of default, about 2.4 log-odds units above those who paid in full, while a one-month delay raises risk only modestly."},{"id":3,"text":"The credit limit (LIMIT_BAL) is the second most important factor, at about 23% of importance: applicants with limits of 90,000 NT dollars or more are predicted to be less risky, with a net effect across the typical range of about -1.1 log-odds units."},{"id":4,"text":"The amount paid in the latest month (PAY_AMT1) is the third most important factor, at about 13.5%, and higher payments are associated with lower predicted default risk, although this effect is smaller and less certain than the first two."},{"id":5,"text":"The interactions matter: the effect of repayment status is weaker for applicants with higher credit limits, and the protective effect of a large credit limit is stronger when repayment status is good than when it is poor, though the uncertainty on these interaction effects is wide."},{"id":6,"text":"The bill amount, age, earlier payment amounts and education each show effects that the data do not reliably distinguish from zero, so we should not read much into them."},{"id":7,"text":"Overall, the model's predictions rest on recent payment behaviour and credit limit, with payment amounts as a secondary signal; the other variables contribute little that can be confidently separated from noise."}]}
